前身為舊高等農林學校作業室，保存磯永吉博士研究與臺大農業發展的歷史。: A former agricultural workshop preserving the history of Dr. Eikichi Iso’s research and agricultural development at NTU.
少了一處承載研究歷史的空間，農田、考種館與休憩空間之間的文化記憶也需要重新串接。: Losing a place that holds research history also changes the cultural connections between farmland, seed research and shared spaces.
保存歷史與研究記憶: Preserve historical buildings and research memories
你把資源優先放在歷史建築與研究故事的保存，讓農場的過去仍能被理解。: You prioritize historic buildings and research stories so the farm’s past remains understandable.
你容易注意時間留下的痕跡。對你來說，一棟老房子不只是建築，而是一段仍存在於現在的: You notice traces left by time. An old house is a memory that remains in the present. New things matter, and so does knowing where we came from.
源自郭錫瑠興建的灌溉系統，農場旁的水源地連結臺北農業歷史與水域生態。: Part of the irrigation system established by Kuo Hsi-liu, connecting Taipei’s agricultural history with the farm’s waterside habitats.
水源與灌溉連結改變，農田及依賴水域、濕潤環境的生命，都可能受到影響。: Changes to water and irrigation may affect farmland and organisms that depend on aquatic or moist habitats.
維護水源與水域環境: Maintain water sources and aquatic habitats
你優先關心水的連結，讓歷史水路與水域生命都有被照顧的機會。: You prioritize the connections made by water, caring for both historical waterways and aquatic life.
很多重要的事情不一定看得見。水可能藏到地下，歷史可能藏進城市。你會去尋找那些仍然: Important connections are not always visible. Water may run underground and history may hide in the city. You seek the threads that still connect everything.
都市中的實驗農地，兼具農業研究、食農教育與田園生活體驗。: Experimental farmland in the city, supporting agricultural research, food education and hands-on rural experiences.
耕作、研究與食農教育少了一個現場；與水、種子、土壤及草地生命的關係也跟著改變。: Farming, research and food education lose a working site, changing connections with water, seeds, soil and grassland life.
維持農作、研究與食農教育: Sustain farming, research and food education
你希望農田持續發揮生產、研究與教育的功能，也思考如何與其他生命共享。: You support farming, research and education while considering how the land can be shared with other life.
你不太想把人與自然分成兩邊。農場可以生產、研究、教育，也可以同時成為其他生命的家: You do not sharply separate people and nature. A farm can produce food, support research and education, and be a home for other life. You ask how we can live together.
前身為綠建築「綠房子」，現作為咖啡廳，讓人休憩、聊天與認識農場。: Formerly the environmentally designed Eco-House, now a café where people can rest, meet and discover the farm.
人們停留、交流的空間減少，也可能改變人與農場、歷史建築和夜間環境互動的方式。: Fewer places to meet and linger may change how people relate to the farm, historic buildings and the nighttime environment.
延續綠建築與交流空間: Continue green architecture and community space
你優先支持人們停留、交流與認識農場的地方，讓舊空間持續有新的用途。: You support a place for meeting, resting and discovering the farm, allowing an old space to serve new purposes.
你是讓事物重新活一次的人: The giver of new life to old places
你接受改變，但改變不一定代表抹掉過去。舊建築可以得到新用途，一個空間也可以重新找: You accept change without erasing the past. An old building can find a new use, and a space can find a new place in our lives.
能精準控制環境的植物研究溫室，支持研究，也需要持續投入能源。: A research greenhouse with precise environmental controls, requiring a continuous investment of energy.
環境控制研究的能力改變，連帶影響種子、農作與植物研究；能源使用也需要重新衡量。: Research capacity changes, with implications for seeds, crops and plant studies. Energy use also needs reconsideration.
支持研究並改善能源使用: Support research and improve energy use
你重視植物研究的能力，也把維護設備、環境控制與能源負擔一起納入考量。: You value plant research while considering equipment maintenance, environmental controls and energy demands together.
當環境出現問題，你傾向問：我們能做什麼？研究、科技、設計與管理，都可能成為回應環: When environmental problems arise, you ask what we can do. Research, technology, design and management can help us respond.
由王大閎設計，因種子檢查需求而興建，現為農藝教學場域之一。: Designed by Wang Dahong for seed testing, the building now supports agronomy education.
種子與農藝教學少了一處場域，農田、研究設施與農業歷史的連結也受到牽動。: Seed and agronomy education lose a venue, weakening links with farmland, research facilities and agricultural history.
保存農藝教學與種子知識: Preserve agronomy education and seed knowledge
你希望延續種子與農藝的知識，替下一代保留學習與研究的場域。: You want seed and agronomy knowledge to continue, retaining places for future learning and research.
你是替未來準備的人: The one preparing for the future
一顆種子很小，但裡面可能藏著整片田地的未來。你做決定時，很容易想到：現在的選擇，: A tiny seed may hold a field’s future. When deciding, you consider what today’s choices will leave for the next generation.
暱稱「洋菇館」，由培育實驗場所轉為土壤博物館，收藏臺灣各地土層剖面標本。: Formerly used for mushroom cultivation, the NTU Soil Museum now houses soil-profile specimens from across Taiwan.
少的是保存與理解土壤的場域，而非土壤本身；農田、種子與土地教育的知識連結可能變弱: What disappears is a place for preserving and understanding soil, not the soil itself. Connections in land education may weaken.
保存土壤標本與土地教育: Preserve soil collections and land education
你支持土壤標本和知識的保存，讓平常不容易看見的土地基礎被理解。: You support soil specimens and knowledge, making the often-hidden foundation of the land easier to understand.
你是看見基礎的人: The one who sees the foundations
你容易注意那些沒有人鼓掌，卻讓整個系統得以存在的東西。土壤、分解者、微生物通常不: You notice what supports a system without receiving applause. Soil, decomposers and microorganisms sustain life from outside the spotlight.
花朵帶有濃香，可提取精油；農場中的香水樹讓人透過氣味認識地方。: Its fragrant flowers can yield essential oil. These trees help people recognize a place through scent.
氣味與季節記憶改變，也少了一處植物與小型生命互動的空間。: Seasonal scents and memories change, and one space for plants and small organisms to interact is lost.
照顧植物與感官記憶: Care for plants and sensory memories
你希望保留植物、氣味與季節的體驗，讓人和地方的感官連結持續存在。: You retain plants, scents and seasonal experiences that connect people to a place.
你不只透過名字認識地方，也在意氣味、季節、光線、聲音，以及身體實際感受到的環境。: You know places through scent, seasons, light, sound and bodily experience, as well as through names.
農場的復育目標之一，期待水源生態系能支持穩定族群，讓夜晚重新出現微光。: A focus of habitat restoration, with the hope that the waterside ecosystem can support a stable population and bring light back to the night.
夜晚少了一種生命，也少了一個讓人關注水源、黑暗與棲地品質的入口。: The night loses one form of life, and an invitation to care about water, darkness and habitat quality.
你優先支持適合螢火蟲生活的環境，把黑暗、水源與減少干擾一起考量。: You support firefly habitat by considering darkness, water and reduced disturbance together.
你容易注意脆弱的環境。有時真正需要保護的不是增加什麼，而是少一點光、少一點干擾，: You notice fragile environments. Sometimes care means less light, less disturbance and more darkness.
夜行性動物，頭頂至鼻尖有白色條紋，夜裡會在校園樹木或電線上活動。: A nocturnal mammal with a white stripe from forehead to nose, moving through campus trees and along wires at night.
夜間活動網絡少了一位成員；人們使用空間的方式與夜行動物共享城市的關係，也值得重新: One participant in the nocturnal network disappears, prompting reflection on how people share the city with wildlife.
你希望城市的夜晚也能容納其他生命，關心夜間活動路徑與人類使用空間的方式。: You want the city at night to accommodate other life, considering animal routes alongside human activities.
你是共享城市的人: The one who shares the city
你知道城市不是只有白天，也不是只屬於人。當我們睡著以後，另一群生命才剛開始牠們的: You know the city is not only a daytime place or a human home. When we sleep, another community begins its day.
眼後有黃色寬縱帶的半水棲龜類，生活在水域及周邊環境，面臨與外來龜類共存的處境。: A semi-aquatic turtle with a yellow stripe behind its eyes, living around water alongside introduced turtle species.
水域少了一種原有生命。即使水還在，棲地中的生命組成與保育意義也已不同。: The water remains, but its community of life and conservation significance have changed.
你優先關心水域及其周邊環境，讓柴棺龜等生命有合適的生活空間。: You prioritize water and its surroundings so turtles and other organisms have suitable places to live.
你是替脆弱生命保留位置的人: The one making room for vulnerable life
你對棲地、界線與消失特別敏感。你會問：在改變發生以前，我們能不能先替牠留下一個位: You notice habitats, boundaries and loss. Before change happens, you ask whether we can leave room for vulnerable life.
常被暱稱為「大笨鳥」或「地瓜」，經常在草地尋找蚯蚓，是校園熟悉的鳥類。: A familiar campus bird, often nicknamed the silly bird or sweet potato, searching for earthworms on lawns.
日常草地景象與覓食關係改變，也提醒我們：常見的生命仍是環境的一部分。: Everyday lawn scenes and feeding relationships change. Common species are still part of the environment.
維護草地與日常鳥類的生活: Care for lawns and everyday birdlife
你選擇照顧常見的生命與草地環境，提醒我們熟悉並不代表不重要。: You care for familiar wildlife and lawns, reminding us that being common does not mean being unimportant.
你是重新看見日常的人: The one who rediscovers the everyday
你知道稀有不是值得珍惜的唯一理由。每天看到的鳥、每天經過的樹，也可能因為太普通而: Rarity is not the only reason to value life. Familiar birds and trees can become so ordinary that we overlook them.
眼旁有黑線的無毒蛇類，會在農場與校園捕食鼠類，是容易被誤解的生命。: A nonvenomous snake with a dark stripe by its eyes. It hunts rodents around the farm and campus and is often misunderstood.
捕食關係少了一環；人與農田、其他生命的共存方式，也需要重新理解。: A link in the feeding network disappears, inviting us to reconsider coexistence between people, farmland and other life.
支持理解、減少誤傷與共存: Support understanding, coexistence and fewer accidental injuries
你願意為容易被害怕的生命留下位置，將辨認、理解與減少誤傷放在前面。: You make room for organisms that people may fear, prioritizing identification, understanding and fewer accidental injuries.
不是所有生命都可愛。有些甚至讓人害怕。但你不會立刻把『喜歡』與『值得存在』畫上等: Not all life seems appealing; some can frighten us. You do not confuse liking an organism with recognizing its place in the world.
斑紋鮮明、個體花紋各異，常在生態豐富的環境中結網，是農場關係網的一部分。: A vividly patterned spider whose markings vary between individuals, weaving webs in biodiverse surroundings.
捕食小型昆蟲的關係改變。移除一個不討喜的節點，也可能牽動其他生命。: Predation on small insects changes. Removing an unpopular organism may also affect other life.
保留結網空間與生態關係: Retain web-building spaces and ecological connections
你關心小型生命的活動空間，也願意看見不一定討喜、卻參與環境關係的角色。: You care about spaces for small organisms and recognize less popular participants in ecological relationships.
你是看見整張網的人: The one who sees the whole web
你不太容易只看一個節點。當一種生命改變，你會自然想到其他生命會怎麼樣。你看見的農: You look beyond a single node. When one organism changes, you consider what happens to others. For you, the farm is an interconnected web.
外來蛙類，背部常見 X 型斑紋，與原生面天樹蛙相似；辨認是理解與管理的第一步。: An introduced frog often marked with an X on its back. It resembles native tree frogs, making careful identification essential.
外來種管理需要先辨認與評估。移除的目標、方法與影響都不同，誤認也可能傷及原生生命: Managing introduced species requires identification and assessment. Targets, methods and consequences differ; mistakes may harm native wildlife.
支持辨識、監測與審慎管理: Support identification, monitoring and careful management
你把資源用在辨識外來種、監測與審慎管理，降低誤認對原生蛙類的影響；這不代表鼓勵外: You invest in identifying introduced species, monitoring and careful management to reduce harm to native frogs. This does not mean encouraging introduced species to spread.
你是先辨認，再決定的人: The one who identifies before deciding
有時最容易犯錯的時刻，就是太快覺得自己已經知道答案。你提醒我們：採取行動以前，先: Mistakes can begin when we assume we already know. You remind us to identify what we are seeing before taking action.

沒有正確答案。系統只記錄：今晚，你怎麼看這座農場。: There is no correct answer. Your choices reflect how you see the farm tonight.
作品從文學院中庭曾經的印度黃檀出發，透過竹構、舊衣布條、手寫故事與編織，讓分散在: Inspired by the Indian rosewood tree once standing in the College of Liberal Arts courtyard, bamboo structures, reused fabric and handwritten stories weave people’s everyday memories into a new shared canopy.

連線包含生態、研究、文化與人的使用關係，是思考示意，不是精確的食物網或實際移除建: Lines represent ecological, research, cultural and human-use connections. This is a reflection exercise, not an exact food web or a recommendation to remove anything.

在正式的「百大貢獻」之外，企劃把目光轉向那些不一定光鮮、未必被稱作重大貢獻，卻真: Beyond celebrated achievements, this project turns to people, events, places, objects and stories that remain in NTU memories. Who decides what deserves to be remembered?
如果不站在聚光燈下，它還重要嗎？: Does something still matter outside the spotlight?
如果只能先保護一項，你會選誰？: If you could protect one thing first, what would it be?

建築可以保存、棲地可以維護，生命也有不同的照顧方式。你選的是資源優先順序。: Buildings can be preserved, habitats maintained, and organisms cared for in different ways. You are choosing a resource priority.
優先支持一項，不代表其他生命或環境元素不重要。: Prioritizing one element does not mean the others are unimportant.
如果一項生命或環境元素不顯眼、不知名，也不容易成為宣傳主角，它是否仍值得投入資源: Does an overlooked or unfamiliar part of the environment still deserve resources?
當資源有限時，哪些生命、空間與記憶會先得到照顧？: When resources are limited, which lives, spaces and memories receive care first?

有些重要的變化，不會第一眼就被看見。: Some important changes are not immediately visible.
「還存在」不等於「沒有承受壓力」: Still present does not mean free from pressure
上一關問的是：誰容易被看見？這一關換一個角度——如果一個族群還沒有消失，但數量持: The last chapter asked who gets noticed. Now consider a population that still exists but is declining as its habitat deteriorates. How long should we wait before acting?
沒有歸零，是否就代表還不用擔心？: Must a population reach zero before we care?

重點不是猜「正確時機」，而是你會如何面對仍存在、卻持續承壓的族群。: Consider how you respond to a population that is still present but under growing pressure.
等到消失，也許太晚。: Waiting until it disappears may be too late.
先處理水、光、土地。: Start with water, light and land.
避免錯誤介入。: Reduce the risk of misguided action.
讓自然有更多調整空間。: Give nature more room to adapt.

數量、棲地與壓力都可能先改變，消失往往只是最後一步。: Numbers, habitats and pressures can change first. Disappearance is often the final step.
一個族群還存在，是否就代表它不需要我們關心？: Does a population’s continued presence mean it needs no care?

If land preserves remains and objects preserve lived experiences, how will the future remember our daily lives?
以老照片、歷史場景與復古攝影回望臺大校園。樹、道路與建築會改變，但影像能把不同年: Old photographs, historical settings and vintage photography revisit NTU. Trees, roads and buildings change, but images bring different eras together, revealing today’s familiar scenes as tomorrow’s history.

自然空間增加，但農作、研究、維護與文化活動也一起變少。: Natural space expands, while farming, research, maintenance and cultural activities decline.
你把唯一的保護幣投給螢火蟲。: You gave your coin to fireflies.
明星物種能吸引人關心環境，但牠也依賴整個棲地。: Popular species can draw attention, but they depend on a whole habitat.
你把保護幣投給檯面下的生命。: You supported life beyond the spotlight.
牠們不顯眼，卻參與分解、土壤形成與養分循環。: Unseen organisms contribute to decomposition, soil formation and nutrient cycles.
保護的不只是個體，也包含牠需要的水域與岸邊環境。: Protection includes both organisms and the water and banks they need.
你替不討喜的生命留了位置。: You made room for unpopular life.
喜不喜歡一種生命，和牠是否值得存在，是兩個不同的問題。: Liking an organism and recognizing its right to exist are different questions.
你沒有把幣投給單一明星。: You supported more than a single star species.
你先改善棲地，試著讓更多生命一起受益。: Improving habitat can benefit many forms of life together.
你不願等到族群歸零才行動，但介入仍需要持續監測。: You will not wait for the population to vanish, but action still requires ongoing monitoring.
你把焦點從單一物種移向水、土地、光線與棲地條件。: You shifted focus from one species to water, land, light and habitat conditions.
你選擇先蒐集更多資料。: You chose to gather more evidence.
更多資料可能降低錯誤介入風險，但等待本身也可能有代價。: Evidence may reduce the risk of mistakes, but waiting can also have a cost.
你留下更多空間給自然調整，也接受結果不完全可控。: You leave nature more room to adjust, accepting that outcomes are not fully controllable.
你選擇重新設計人的使用方式。: You chose to redesign human use.
不是把人完全移除，而是重新安排不同生命如何共享空間。: You rethink how different forms of life can share space, rather than removing people entirely.
你封存了老建築與農業研究。: You preserved old buildings and agricultural research.
一棟建築，也可能留下某個時代如何理解土地與農業的痕跡。: A building can retain traces of how an era understood land and farming.
你封存了水的記憶。: You preserved the memory of water.
水路即使從地表消失，也可能留在地名、地形與地方故事裡。: A vanished waterway may remain in place names, landforms and local stories.
耕作、土壤與食物來源看似普通，也構成城市歷史。: Farming, soil and food sources are ordinary but also form urban history.
你封存了夜晚的感官。: You preserved the senses of the night.
氣味、蛙鳴、黑暗與夜行生命，也能成為地方被記住的方法。: Scents, frog calls, darkness and nocturnal life help us remember a place.
真正陪伴我們最久的，常常不是大事件，而是每天重複的小事。: What stays with us longest is often not a great event, but small things repeated every day.
被埋藏不代表不存在。考古也是替失去聲音的事物留下記憶。: Being buried does not mean never existing. Archaeology preserves memories of things that can no longer speak.
你把舞台中央留給人。: You put people at centre stage.
校園承載人的學習與生活；問題是，其他生命需要的空間放在哪裡？: Campus supports human learning and daily life. Where does that leave space for other organisms?

牠們沒有參與規劃，卻一直承受人類做出的空間決定。: Other organisms never joined the planning, yet live with the effects of human decisions about space.
你取消了唯一主角。: You removed the single leading role.
沒有固定中心後，空間必須持續協商不同生命的需求。: Without a fixed centre, the needs of different forms of life must be continually negotiated.
你讓舞台隨時間輪替。: You let the stage change with time.
同一個地方，白天與夜晚可能屬於完全不同的使用者。: The same place may have entirely different users by day and by night.
你把聚光燈移向日常。: You turned the spotlight toward the everyday.
平凡並不代表不重要，有些生命只是因為太常見而被忽略。: Ordinary does not mean unimportant. Familiarity can make life easy to overlook.
中心被拿掉，空間可以依時間、需求與環境重新安排。: Without a fixed centre, space can adapt to time, needs and environmental conditions.
未來的進步，也許不只是增加更多光，而是知道什麼時候可以不照亮。: Progress may mean knowing when to leave a place unlit, rather than adding more light.
一條水路同時是景觀、歷史，也可能是許多生命的棲地。: A waterway is landscape, history and potentially a home for many forms of life.
即使城市高度發展，土地仍能提醒人們食物從哪裡來。: Even in a developed city, land can remind people where food comes from.
